title: Resolution Due Dates, Notices and Extensions of Appeals and Grievances Cases
content:
This part of the **Appeals and Grievances** policy manual governs the resolution due date of a case, the notice of resolution and the extension of the due date.

## Clauses

**1. Resolution period.** A case is resolved within the case type's resolution period, read in that case type's unit (calendar days or hours), of the filed date.

**2. Resolution notice.** Written notice of the resolution is mailed within the case type's resolution notice period in business days, with oral notice as well where the case type gives the resolution orally. Resolving a case records the resolved date and the outcome, and logs a resolution notice letter dated the resolved date.

**3. Extension.** The due date may be extended once by up to the case type's extension ceiling when the member asks or the plan shows the extension is in the member's interest, with written notice within the case type's extension notice period and notice of the right to grieve the extension. An extension records the new due date and the reason, and logs an extension notice letter.

**4. Extension cutoff.** An extension is taken no later than 0 days after the case's current due date. The cutoff is counted in calendar days from the due date, so an extension on the due date itself still qualifies. The current due date is read from the plan's record of that case, before the extension is taken.

**5. One extension only.** A case already extended once is never extended again.

## Conditions for an extension, restated

| Condition | Must hold |
|---|---|
| The member asks for the extension, or the plan shows it is in the member's interest | One of the two |
| The extension is taken on or before the case's current due date | Yes |
| The case has not been extended before | Yes |
| The new due date lies no more than the case type's extension ceiling after the current due date | Yes |

An extension that is taken is accompanied by written notice within the extension notice period, together with notice of the member's right to grieve the extension.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

| Case's current due date | Day the extension is taken | Qualifies under the cutoff |
|---|---|---|
| A given day D | The day before D | Yes |
| A given day D | D itself | Yes |
| A given day D | The day after D | No: 0 days after the due date is the last qualifying day |

## Hypothetical illustrations

- A case type with a 14-day ceiling: extending the due date by 10 calendar days is within the ceiling, and by 20 calendar days is not.
- A case that was extended once and is approaching its new due date: it is never extended again, whoever asks.
- A case type whose extension ceiling is 0: no extension is allowed.
